title: Tanzanian Spinach Curry
community: Urban Tanzania — the spiced spinach preparation
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Mchicha wa Curry — spinach or amaranth leaves sautéed in a fragrant onion, tomato, and spice base with cumin, turmeric, and coconut milk. The Indian Ocean-influenced spiced spinach preparation — more aromatic and deeply flavoured than plain sautéed greens.
longDesc: The spiced spinach curry reflects Tanzania's Indian Ocean trading heritage — the same spice tradition that perfumes the pilau and the biriani is applied to the everyday spinach, creating a vegetable dish of unusual depth and fragrance.
ingredients: 500g fresh spinach or mchicha — washed and roughly chopped
steps: Heat oil. Cook onions until golden.
Add garlic, ginger, and all spices. Stir 1 minute.
Add tomatoes. Cook 6 minutes until thick.
Add spinach in batches. Stir until wilted.
Pour in coconut milk. Simmer gently 6—8 minutes.
chefTips: Add spinach in batches — the first batch must wilt before the next goes in.
Coconut milk makes this richer than plain sautéed spinach.
Do not boil the coconut milk hard.
commonMistakes: Adding all spinach at once — too much volume to stir.
cookingScience: Spinach contains oxalic acid which inhibits calcium absorption. The vitamin C in the tomatoes simultaneously increases iron absorption — the two effects partially balance each other, resulting in a dish with better overall mineral bioavailability than spinach alone.
sustainabilityTips: Locally grown Tanzanian spinach and coconut.
culturalNote: Spiced spinach curry reflects the multilayered food culture of Tanzania's coast — where African vegetables meet Indian Ocean spice in daily cooking.
